title: Ternary vectorial dual-bent functions with negative sign
summary: Decide whether the source's negative-sign Condition C branch exists for output dimension at least two.

formal_statement.body: For $p=3$ and $m\ge2$, does there exist an admissible $F:V_n(3)\to\mathbb F_{3^m}$ satisfying the source's Condition C with common sign $\varepsilon=-1$ and $(3^m-1)\mid d$? A single explicit witness settles the positive direction; a proof of nonexistence settles the negative direction.

scope.domain: Ternary vectorial dual-bent functions and their Condition C sign/divisibility parameters
assumptions: F: V_n(3) -> F_{3^m} satisfies every requirement of Condition C
The common-sign case is (A.1) with epsilon=-1
scope.unresolved_remainder: No explicit witness or nonexistence theorem is known for any m >= 2 satisfying the full Condition C, epsilon=-1, and (3^m-1) | d requirements.

citations.label: Wang--Wei--Fu--Li, Self-Orthogonal Codes From Vectorial Dual-Bent Functions

progress.summary: Remark 3(i) explicitly leaves the m >= 2 negative-sign existence question open while noting a scalar ternary example.
